what: The big title’s letters start faint (.2), then from when the title top reaches 90% of the screen until the title middle reaches 40%, they are tied to scroll and darken in order from the first letter (.1 between letters, no curve). Words painted in the accent color darken in the same order. Scrolling back up fades them again.

options.unit: If “words”, it darkens word by word in turn (default is letters)
options.scrub: Scroll-follow delay in seconds, default immediate (true) — Name .4
options.line: (If present) delays each line’s start by this much (scroll share) — breath between lines, brand .4
options.dur: Length over which one letter darkens (same unit as the sequence), default .5 — the longer it is, the more letters blur together
options.lead: Blank share before the first character (same unit), default 0 — stays put briefly even after entering the range
options.span: Front share of the start→end range used for fading in, default 1 — at .6 it is fully opaque at 60% of the range
options.track: (if present) measures the nearest ancestor found with this css — when the text sits inside a sticky panel, it uses that panel’s long outer span (exalt [data-reveal-track])
options.tint: If 1, change the text color instead of fading — from --fx-tint-from (css, default --kf-dim) to the element’s own text color (gray → white, as in the original)
options.--fx-tint-from: Initial text color of tint (css), default var(--kf-dim)

use: Your Big Headline Here Highlighted Word Continuing sentence
note: SplitText autoSplit, so it splits again when a late-loading font changes the line breaks. Words are inline-block chunks, so Korean line breaks never cut in the middle of a word
